Tanzania Plans to Lift Export Ban On Sea Fish
Africa News
March 8, 2004 Monday


Copyright 2004 AllAfrica, Inc.
Length: 473 words
Byline: The East African
Body


Some 20 marine fishing vessels have been permitted to export fish products, but these are restricted to prawns, crabs and lobsters
TANZANIA IS planning to lift the ban on exports of sea fish and fish products caught in its Indian Ocean waters.
At the time of the imposition of the ban two years ago, Tanzania's ocean waters had been invaded by over 70 foreign illegal trawlers that were fishing for tuna and other species off the Rufiji river delta and Mafia Island.
The trawlers, fitted with fish processing plants, exported the catch directly without paying any revenue to the government. The government sought the help of the South African and French navy to keep the illegal trawlers away from its coast.
The government then banned fishing trawlers, saying they were not only depleting fish stocks, but also destroying the coral rocks that serve as breeding grounds for most of the fish caught by artisanal fishermen.
To date, the Ministry of Natural Resources says 20 marine fishing vessels have been permitted to export fish products, but these are restricted to prawns, crabs and lobsters caught mainly in the Rufiji river delta and areas between the river delta and Mafia Island.
The Assistant Director of Fisheries in the Ministry of Natural Resources, Winfried V. Haule, told The EastAfrican last week that the government held its first meeting on lifting the ban on fish exports last December in Dar es Salaam, which focused on the utilisation of marine water exports.
The meeting brought together officials from the Ministry of Natural Resources, members of parliament from the coastal belt, regional and district commissioners and officials from other government departments. A follow up meeting is scheduled for this April.
"I cannot give the exact date when the government will endorse the export of marine water products, but it will be very soon," said Mr Haule.
The Directorate of Fisheries is proposing to reduce the prawn fishing season beginning 2005 from nine to six months, to run between April and October to give the prawns more time to breed. The current fishing season runs from March to November.
The country has three other potential prawn fishing areas in Bagamoyo north of Dar es Salaam and Kisiju and Kilwa in Coast Region south of Dar es Salaam.
Tanzania has 1.04 per cent of the world's total reefs and its marine and inland fishery resources produce an estimated 730,000 tonnes of fish annually.
Apart from the Indian Ocean, Tanzania also has the waters of Lakes Victoria, Tanganyika and Nyasa, which it shares with its neighbours. It also has diverse river systems, and numerous wetlands.
The fisheries sector in Tanzania accounts for 10 per cent of gross domestic product. According to 1998 research findings, prawn fishing supports over 25,000 people directly.
